name: Bhoramdeo Temple (Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh)
best_time: October to March (Bhoramdeo Mahotsav in spring)
rules: Footwear removal required at stone plinth base
Admire the 11th-century Nagara style stone carvings of the Nagavanshi dynasty
visual_features: exquisite 11th-century stone temple standing on a five-foot platform nestled against the dense forested backdrop of the Maikal mountain range
description: Bhoramdeo Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to the god Shiva in Bhoramdeo, in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh. It comprises a group of four temples of which the earliest is a brick-temple. The main temple is the Bhoramdeo temple built in stone. The architectural features with erotic sculptures has given a distinct style akin to the Khajuraho temple and the Konark Sun Temple in Odisha, and hence the Bhoramdeo complex is known by the sobriquet the "Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh".
